Liquid AI vs Jev: When Decision Models Can See and Hear
Turing Post TV · October 9, 2026 · youtube.com

What happens when AI can see, hear, and make decisions right on a device? Liquid AI’s new open-weight decision models bring that question into the physical world.

In this episode of Attention Span, Ksenia explores Open d1: what these small models do, how they differ from Jev, and why local decision-making matters for robotics, assistive devices, and autonomous laboratories.

We start with a hand-controlled game of Flappy Bird – and follow the idea all the way to machines making useful judgments about their surroundings.

Along the way:
What decision models actually do
d1-3B and d1-omni-600M: vision, audio, and open weights
What happened to Liquid’s original liquid neural networks
Why a small model isn’t automatically fast on your hardware
What Liquid’s NVIDIA Jetson results tell us
Where demos end and the challenges of physical AI begin

*Subscribe to Attention Span by Turing Post* for clear explanations of AI research, the ideas behind it, and what they mean in practice. If this episode helped something click, like it and share it with someone building with AI.
